full_judgment: 13. Requirement to deposit the penalty by a PSI agent under section 194(1) of the Customs Act has been considered thoroughly and exhaustively in the case of Intertek Testing Service (BD) Limited vs President, Appellate Tribunal, Customs, Excise & VAT, Dhaka, reported in 57 DLR 74. In deciding the issue, a Division Bench of this court after meticulous discussions observed as follows: 37) First, the Act was promulgated in 1969. Under section 156 of the Act various offences or punishments under 98 categories are described and/or provided. Under the Act other penalty may also be possible to be imposed. By the expression, "under the Act" the legislature clearly intended to include any such penalty imposed under section 156 or any other provision of the Act. Had the legislature ever intended to include a penalty levied under the Order, it could have come out with appropriate amendment. 38) Not Relevant. 39) Second, intention of the Government also becomes clearer if we examine the definition of the Act in the Order itself. In the Order, article 2(Ga) clearly says that the Act means the Customs Act. The Government was very conscious of its limitation that when the legislature did not expand the Act to include the Order, it had no jurisdiction to mean the Order as the Act.
